chunks: And they say: 'These are fables of antiquity he has invented, which are dictated to him morning and evening.'
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers claim about the source of the Quran in Surah Al-Furqan?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the persistent skepticism of the Meccan polytheists who reduced the Quran's profound theological depth to mere 'asatir' (ancient fables) compiled by the Prophet. The phrase 'bukratan wa asila' (morning and evening) emphasizes the continuous, almost mechanical nature of their accusation, contrasting human fabrication with the divine, uncreated speech of Allah. This critique serves as a foundational argument for the Quran's miraculous nature, refuting the claim that it was a human literary construct.
